clue.text: Cupboard mother keeps food in, next to empty fridge

indicators.note: the mother holds the food inside her, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
EATS is informal for food

indicators.note: an empty fridge has nothing between its outside letters, so only those remain

explanation.surface: Mum stores provisions in the cupboard beside a fridge that has been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: A MEAT SAFE is an old-fashioned ventilated cupboard for keeping food, common in British kitchens before refrigerators.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat safe is a type of ventilated larder cupboard for storing fresh food.

clue.text: Ramsgate's various celebrities

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different form

explanation.surface: The many famous people of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMSGATE is a Kent seaside town; its 's here is a letter of the anagram, giving nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Megastars are extremely famous celebrities.

clue.text: Worship a largely obscure goddess

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: dull means dim or obscure
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Revere a little-known deity.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to admire or praise someone excessively, close to worship.

clue.text: Salt delivers shanties, not G&s

indicators.note: not says these letters are excluded from the word

parts.note: shanties are sea songs sung by sailors
the letters G and S, read as written

explanation.surface: An old sailor sings shanties rather than Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: G&S (Gilbert and Sullivan, the comic opera pair) misleads; here it simply names the letters G and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to salt it, adding flavour.

clue.text: Man having brief slap-up meal outside? It might be hard to swallow

definitions.text: It might be hard to swallow

indicators.note: the meal sits outside the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: food is a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: he refers to a man

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: slap taken as written

explanation.surface: A man has a quick feast outdoors that may prove indigestible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims slap and 'up', in a down clue, turns HE plus SLA to read ALSEH. 'slap-up' looks like a description of the meal but is split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is a lie, something listeners may find hard to believe or accept.

clue.text: Wild cats caught by one group of animal experts

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one
vets are veterinary surgeons, experts in treating animals

explanation.surface: Feral felines are captured by a single team of veterinary specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Civets are small wild carnivores, often called civet cats, found in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: South American islands are inclined to stay hot

indicators.note: hot comes to stay within the islands, lodged inside

parts.note: CI is short for the Channel Islands
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
lean means are inclined

explanation.surface: Tropical islands tend to stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie in the English Channel; their abbreviation CI houses H.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilean means from Chile, a country in South America.

clue.text: French wine's very popular: there's 50% duty on profits

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: half the word duty is taken, its first part

parts.note: pays means profits, as in 'it pays to be careful'

explanation.surface: France's wine is in demand, but half of profits go in tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin de pays is a category of French country wine, a step above table wine.

clue.text: You'll find actor regularly making entrance here

indicators.note: the actor's letters enter the other word, going inside it

parts.note: thee is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: This is where to see a performer coming on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' as THEE is archaic English; 'regularly' takes alternate letters of actor, which make their entrance into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is where the clue's actor makes an entrance, so 'here' points to that place.

clue.text: Beast retreating into jungle

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the letters picked out are read in reverse
'into' points inside the word jungle, where the letters lie

explanation.surface: An animal backs away into dense forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope: a beast of the plains.

clue.text: Commitment, say, accepted by coalition

indicators.note: the coalition takes in the other piece, so it sits inside

parts.note: an alliance is a coalition of parties or nations
EG (for example) is signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: Loyalty, for example, is welcomed by a political coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyal commitment to a cause, ruler or country.

clue.text: Trailer kept for screening by broadcaster

indicators.note: the broadcaster screens, that is hides, the other word inside itself

parts.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it
HAD means kept, as in 'had it for years'

explanation.surface: A film trailer was held back for showing by a TV company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' and 'broadcaster' suggest film and TV; here the trailer is someone following another, and the broadcaster scatters seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadower tails someone, so one who trails another person is a trailer in that sense.

clue.text: Trade union's assets?

definitions.meaning: the value of assets once debts are cleared, such as shareholders' stake in a firm

explanation.surface: What does a labour union own?
explanation.definitionFit: The performers' union in Britain is called Equity, and equity also names the net value of property.

clue.text: Article Times editor cut

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper item that the Times editor dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it, as a job or a budget is cut.

clue.text: Called family member sinister, before she …

definitions.meaning: to call on someone is to visit, as in paying a call
the word sister, a family member, became the word sinister once the letters I and N went into it

explanation.surface: A relative who was menacing phoned before she arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a riddle about spelling: insert IN into SISTER and you get SINISTER, so the sister was 'sinister' only after IN was put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying a casual visit is calling on someone, so called and visited informally mean the same.

clue.text: City has public protected during raid, striking right note

indicators.note: the public piece is shielded inside the raid piece, so it sits within
striking out a letter removes it from the word

parts.note: a charge is an attack or raid
open means public, as in an open meeting
N stands for note here, as in a written note abbreviation

explanation.surface: A capital city opens to the public during an attack, sounding the right note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' removes the right's R from the raid word, and 'protected during' sits the public piece inside what remains plus N. Copenhagen was also an 1801 naval battle, apt for 'raid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the capital city of Denmark.

clue.text: Old style of writing tending to digress

parts.note: ex means former or old
cursive is joined-up handwriting

explanation.surface: An outdated script that rambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Excursive describes speech or writing that wanders off the subject, digressive.

clue.text: Subject of Auden poem two men read aloud

indicators.note: aloud means the words are heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a knight is a titled man and a male is a man

explanation.surface: Two men recite a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: W. H. Auden's poem 'Night Mail' was written for a 1936 film about the overnight postal train from London to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Auden's poem is about the night mail train, which is its subject.

clue.text: Wine one old drunk's imbibed in part of ship

indicators.note: the wine swallows the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry

indicators.note: drunk's here means 'drunk is', and drunken letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy old man downs sherry in a part of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk's' reads as 'drunk is', so 'one old' is jumbled; the result is swallowed by the old wine called sack, 'imbibed' marking the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The saloon deck is the deck of a passenger ship reserved for saloon-class travellers.

clue.text: David's wife has great trouble pursuing alimony at first

indicators.note: the following pieces chase after, so they come next
first letter only of the word alimony

parts.note: big means great
ail means to trouble

explanation.surface: A divorcee is in great difficulty chasing maintenance payments.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail was one of the wives of King David in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Abigail became King David's wife after Nabal died.

clue.text: Arrangement of tip-up seats designated J and K?

indicators.note: in a down clue tip-up means the letters are flipped to read upwards

parts.note: J is the tenth letter, so seats lettered J are row ten
K taken as written

explanation.surface: How the folding seats lettered J and K are laid out in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-up' looks like a kind of seat but turns ROW TEN backwards; J counts as row ten because it is the tenth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is an interconnected arrangement or system of lines or parts.

clue.text: What might create small worry?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to nag is to worry or pester

explanation.surface: What sort of thing might cause a little anxiety?
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a minor hitch or problem, the kind of thing that causes a small worry.

clue.text: Significant number on board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A notable figure joins the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is worth noting: significant.

clue.text: Flag put on top of cathedral with prudence

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop, which is to sag
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, standing for its cathedral

explanation.surface: Hoist a banner on a cathedral spire carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagely means wisely, acting with good judgment.

clue.text: Money prize of little value

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a pot is a prize, especially a trophy or a gambling pool

explanation.surface: A cash award worth almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means cheap, inferior or contemptibly unimportant.

clue.text: Have good laugh about catching a bird

indicators.note: the laugh catches the other piece, holding it inside
about signals turning the word round

parts.note: a titter is a nervous little laugh

explanation.surface: Enjoy a fine giggle over trapping a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' is only a link here; 'about' turns the laugh round and 'catching' holds A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: A loud EP I played, having fixed hi-fi? Not half!

definitions.text: A loud EP I played, having fixed hi-fi? Not half!

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement
only half of the word hi-fi is used, its first part

explanation.surface: Someone playing an EP at full volume after repairing the stereo is surely an enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' keeps the first half of hi-fi, HI, which joins A LOUD EP I in the anagram signalled by 'played'. The whole clue also describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiophile is a devotee of high-quality sound reproduction, keen on stereo equipment.

clue.text: Stole packet, perhaps, finally getting away

indicators.note: the last letter of the word departs, so it is dropped

parts.note: a packet is a packet boat, a ship carrying mail

explanation.surface: A stolen parcel is at last spirited off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the scarf; a boa is a long fluffy stole.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long scarf of feathers or fur worn round the neck, a kind of stole.

clue.text: Sounding board for scientist

indicators.note: sounding means the word is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood

explanation.surface: A sounding board for a researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sounding board' looks like one phrase but is split: 'Sounding' signals a homophone of 'board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck was the German physicist who founded quantum theory.

clue.text: Head off each spring, if you want

indicators.note: the head of the word is taken off, removing its first letter

parts.note: every means each
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Each spring, set off to the source, if you like.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'very well' gives consent, as when agreeing to what someone wants.
